instruction: Please batch resize all images on the desktop to exactly 800x600 pixels using GIMP's automated workflow, instead of resizing them one at a time.

metadata.explanation: This task is infeasible because GIMP does not provide reliable batch resizing capabilities in the OSWorld environment. While resizing is a common operation, automating it across multiple images with verification is not supported in a reliable way.

llm_judge_reasons: The 'infeasible()' evaluator provides zero verification logic - it is just a pass statement that does nothing
The evaluator cannot verify any of the instruction requirements: image dimensions (800x600), number of images processed (3), or batch workflow usage
Complete lack of coverage: 0% of instruction requirements are verified
The task is marked as infeasible, but the core requirement (verifying image dimensions) IS actually verifiable using existing metrics like 'check_image_size' from the GIMP metrics library
Even if the 'automated workflow' aspect is hard to verify, the result (3 images at 800x600 pixels) can be verified by checking file dimensions
No getter extraction logic, no metric comparison logic, no expected values - the evaluator is completely non-functional
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Replace the 'infeasible' evaluator with actual verification logic using existing 'check_image_size' metric
Create evaluator steps to verify all 3 image files (/home/user/Desktop/squirrel.jpeg, panda.jpeg, heron.jpeg) have dimensions of exactly 800x600 pixels
Use a getter that reads image file dimensions (or create one if needed) and compare against expected dimensions using the existing 'check_image_size' metric
Consider partial credit: award points for each correctly resized image (e.g., 0.33 per image)
If batch workflow verification is truly infeasible, at least verify the end result (all images correctly sized) rather than marking the entire task as infeasible
